title: To-do & project planning

body.text: Throw a big goal at the AI and have it break it into
a plan: subtasks, sequence, durations, and milestones
— e.g. 'organize a seminar for 200 people in 2 months' gives you a checklist with a timeline you can start on right away.

example: "Plan opening an online store in 6 weeks, broken into weekly tasks, noting which can run in parallel and which have to wait"

title: A good plan finds the risks first

body.text: Add value by asking for a
pre-mortem: if this project failed, what would the likely causes be
— the AI points out risks you overlooked, then you build the safeguards into the timeline from the start.

example: "Suppose this seminar failed — what are the 3 most likely causes, and how do we prevent each from week one?"

question: How does the AI help plan a project?

options.text: Breaks the goal into subtasks, sequence, and a timeline
Does the whole project for you
Imagining it has failed, then finding the causes in advance
A meeting after the project ends

question: What information makes a plan usable in reality?

options.text: Noting which tasks run in parallel and which depend on others
Putting every task on the last day

question: What should good project planning include?

options.text: Listing tasks, sequence, and risks in advance

question: What does 'a good plan finds the risks first' mean?

options.text: No need to think about risks
Anticipate problems and prepare to handle them
Wait for the problem to happen first
